descriptions.text: Standard Healing Potion. Increases your health by at least 50%. Doesn’t cure poison or other health-seeping conditions such as succubus-inflicted gonorrhea. So remember to wrap it up, bucko.

beats.headline: A gift from Mordecai
beats.text: Mordecai produces a single glass bottle, small, about a third the size of a Coke bottle, red with a cork in it: a gift from him to Carl. Carl examines it, adds it to his inventory, which now has a Potions and Healing submenu, and pulls it back into his hand with a mental click. Put it on your hotlist, Mordecai tells him, and you will drink it without having to actually drink. Then his boxes open: one bronze adventurer box holds two more potions of healing, and another one more.

beats.headline: Kiwi juice and poison
beats.text: Donut is soaked in blood and barely alive. The Heal Critter scroll will not work on her, and Carl does not know where her potion countdown stands: she took a mana potion a few minutes ago. So he tests on himself. The quick slots won't let him take a second potion. He drinks one by hand, his first time physically drinking one, and it tastes oddly like kiwi juice. Then he drinks a second before the fifteen-second timer is done. You have been poisoned! Poison effect nullified.

beats.headline: Against the undead
beats.text: The Cookbook's explosives section carries a note from Crawler Sinjin of the fifteenth edition: a level 3 sapper's table lets you infuse bombs, and a hobgoblin smoke curtain soaked in a healing potion and left to dry mass-kills undead like you wouldn't believe. Crawler Forkith of the twentieth confirms it. It works with bombs too, but smoke works better, and high-level undead only get mad.

beats.headline: Napalm for vampires
beats.text: Mordecai has an idea before they leave: two potion balls, dipped in the red water of the Emberus shrine at the back of the room. The system labels them Holy Goopers. Blessed water, a fine healing potion and an air-activated coagulant: Emberus is a light-based god, and against vampires the mixture acts like napalm. Hit them with it, he says, then have Donut max out her Torch spell.

beats.headline: Into the fog
beats.text: A park several blocks wide is filled with red dots and roiling fog, and Sister Ines, who can tell whether a mob is undead, says all of them are. Levitating for a view, Carl tosses a potion ball filled with a fine healing potion into a dense patch of red. Three of the mobs die, easily and soundlessly, for very little experience, and he tells the others they are good to go.

beats.headline: Set to two percent
beats.text: Carl's new Legendary toe ring, which must go on his left pinky toe and says so twice, can store one potion that triggers itself when his health meets a condition. He grits his teeth, slips the ring on, and is prompted to choose. He picks a gold-standard healing potion, set to trigger if his health reaches two percent.

relations.note: no countdown between scrolls, where potions have one
